items.text: Channel 13 Israel reported that the Israeli army is preparing for the possibility of ballistic missile and drone attacks from Yemen amid escalating conflicts and developments in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The main concern is the Houthi attacks on ships and their impact on global trade. The Israeli army is also examining the consequences of Yemen's developments on tensions between the US and the Islamic Republic in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abed Alizadeh, a citizen from Takab, was released today from Miandoab prison after posting bail.

During the seventh week of the Premier League, fans of Sanat Naft Abadan chanted against their coach Mohammad Nouri. The match against Chadormalu Ardakan was held at Takhti Abadan Stadium. Sanat Naft lost the game 2-1 and is at the bottom of the league table.

The Turkish Treasury Minister stated that payments for gas imported from Iran are not made directly to the Islamic Republic but are held in an account with strict regulations. Iran can only use this account to pay for authorized goods. Turkey cooperates with the US to combat money laundering and sanctions evasion.

Due to lack of workplace safety, two workers in Khondab and Bandar Mahshahr were involved in accidents. One worker died and another was injured. These incidents were reported to be caused by unsafe working conditions.

The appeals court reduced the prison sentence of Ali Mokhtari, a researcher and PhD student in public law at Beheshti University, to six months. Four months of this sentence have been suspended. He was previously sentenced to 18 months in prison.

Ali Cheldavi, a 13-year-old Arab child from Ahvaz, was arrested by the Intelligence Organization of the IRGC in the village of Oboudeh, Ahvaz. Mustafa Cheldavi and at least 10 other Sunni Arab citizens were also detained in this operation. Families are concerned about the detainees' condition, and the Karun Human Rights Organization has called for their release and clarification of their detention locations.

Ghassan Ashour stated that the Houthis have agreed not to attack US and other countries' ships except Saudi Arabia. He said they see this as an opportunity for military advancement. They may change their tactics in the future.

Abba Bush, Sweden's Deputy Prime Minister, called for increased financial and economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He also emphasized that the Swedish government must protect Iranians residing in the country from threats by the Islamic Republic. He urged practical action to stop executions and political trials.

The US President emphasized strong control and a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz during a meeting with the Irish Prime Minister. He stated that CENTCOM forces stop an average of 25 vessels daily. CENTCOM announced that in the past 60 days, the routes of 100 commercial ships have been changed.

Shahram Khaledi stated that the Islamic Republic's actions in the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on regional energy infrastructure have led to a regional and international consensus against Tehran. He added that for years, the Islamic Republic has sought to impose its model on the Persian Gulf by disrupting regional security. This approach has faced opposition from regional countries and will ultimately fail.

Ricardo Sa Pinto, former coach of Esteghlal, criticized Ali Tajernia's interference in the team's lineup and player selections. He said Tajernia tried to impose a player named Ali Shojaei on him, which he refused. Sa Pinto also claimed that Saeed Fattahi was added to Esteghlal to manage relations with referees.

Real Madrid defeated Rayo Vallecano 4-1 in the fifth week of La Liga with a double from Kylian Mbappe and goals from Alvaro Carreras and Jude Bellingham. With their fourth win in five games, they are now level on points with Barcelona. Barcelona can retake the top spot if they win against Levante.

Masoud Pezeshkian reacted to the US economic pressures on Iran by calling for direct confrontation with US military forces. He questioned why the US wages war against civilian infrastructure and people's livelihoods. He also criticized depriving people of water, food, and medicine.

Mithaq Zareh said at the Venice Film Festival that government repression in Iran has caused despair and numbness among people. He emphasized that cinema has become a weapon against censorship. The film "A Little Light" tells the story of a doctor who decides to end his life after being arrested but finds new reasons to live.

Kambiz Tavana stated that increased Houthi influence over Bab al-Mandab could strengthen the Islamic Republic's regional leverage. He added that over 10 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz in the past seven days. No Iranian oil tankers were seen in this data.

Bijan Kian described the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast as a tactical victory that could lead to a new coalition against the Islamic Republic. He also said the US is no longer willing to pay for regional security without strategic alignment with regional countries. Saudi Arabia and Gulf states must decide on their future relations with Tehran and Washington.

Hassan Mansour stated that the Islamic Republic's foreign exchange resources do not meet commercial needs. He warned that reduced imports could lead to shortages of essential goods. Additionally, the existing foreign exchange resources are not stable or reliable.

Laleh Marzban won the Best Actress award in the Horizons section at the Venice International Film Festival. The film, directed by Mohsen Gharaei, tells the story of a girl who wants to travel to Turkey but is confined at home by her father. Marzban dedicated her award to Iranian women and urged people not to lose hope.

Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the US Open final to win her third Grand Slam title. With this victory, she rose to the world number one ranking and ended Sabalenka's 20-match winning streak. Despite an ankle injury, Rybakina added the US Open trophy to her previous Australian Open and Wimbledon titles.

The Yemeni army targeted Houthi positions in Taiz with airstrikes. The Houthis attacked a military base in the Sharurah area of Saudi Arabia with drones and ballistic missiles. A projectile landing in Jazan, Saudi Arabia, injured two people and caused damage to civilian infrastructure.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. A ship was targeted by an unknown projectile while passing through the strait. The crew's condition and damages are currently unknown, and investigations are ongoing.

Esmail Kowsari and Vahid Ahmadi stated that no proposal regarding Iran's exit from the NPT has been submitted to the National Security Commission. Ahmadi emphasized that this issue should be reviewed by the commission, and the parliament has no sessions this week. Earlier, a representative announced the preparation of a proposal to exit the NPT.

On the early morning of Sunday, 22 Shahrivar, continuous gunfire was heard near police stations and military bases in the Bakhshan area of Saravan. The gunfire was one-sided, and the cause and type of weapon are unknown. This report came after a 9-hour clash between military forces and armed individuals affiliated with the People's Fighters Front.

The International Organization for Migration reported that at least 76,000 people have been displaced since July due to intensified clashes along Yemen's Red Sea coast. The number of displaced people has quadrupled in the past week, with 30,000 added in just a few days. Additionally, about 1,400 people entered Djibouti from Yemen within 24 hours.

Reduction of subsidies and fuel quotas in Iran has caused dissatisfaction and strikes among truck and taxi drivers. Long queues have formed at fuel stations. The government faces economic difficulties and pressures from sanctions.

Alexey Likhachov stated that 47 Rosatom specialists have returned to the Bushehr nuclear power plant, with plans to increase to 150. Scheduled maintenance for fuel assembly replacement will begin in mid-September. Construction of the second and third units and repairs of the first unit at Bushehr are also underway.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the Islamic Republic should officially declare that in case of an attack on any Iranian tanker, all tankers within range will be targeted. This could lead to a reduction in operational tankers and a historic increase in oil prices. Kayhan emphasized the need for precise planning and use of military and economic capacities for aggressive deterrence.

Abbas Goudarzi, spokesperson of the Parliament's presidium, said that Iran's exit from the NPT and reconsideration of its nuclear doctrine would put the US in its place. He called negotiations with the US a strategic mistake that would weaken the resistance front. Goudarzi described the conflict between Iran and the US as intrinsic and fundamental.

Amir Teymouri, governor of Qeshm, announced that an Iranian commercial ship was hit around 5 AM on Sunday, September 12, near Hengam Island and the Shib Deraz coast of Qeshm Island. One person was killed and three were injured in the incident.

Hussein Mozaffari, the Friday prayer leader of Qazvin, described chastity and hijab as national and religious symbols and emphasized their preservation. He stated that society is influenced by the enemy's negative propaganda. Mozaffari stressed confronting the cultural conspiracies of the enemy.

Ahmad Nadari, a member of the parliament's presidium, stated that Iran's strategy in the Persian Gulf is based on ambiguity, deterrence, and strategic surprise. He added that there are surprises for the US that have not yet been unveiled. Nadari also emphasized that confrontation with the US is not only based on military power but also involves changing the opponent's calculations.

Mohammad Qaedi commented on the meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Muscat and the agreement between Iran and Oman on a joint route in the Strait of Hormuz. He said the meeting currently holds more symbolic importance. It may also pave the way for future security agreements.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in an interview with India Today that Iran is currently not ready for direct talks with Donald Trump because their leader was killed. He added that building trust is necessary for negotiations. Pezeshkian also said Iran is not at war with Saudi Arabia and there is no reason for conflict among regional countries.

Ali Dadpay stated that the reduction in exports and limited access of the Islamic Republic to foreign currency resources decreases the ability to pay and transport goods. Using land routes cannot replace sea routes due to limited capacity and high transportation costs. Increased import costs and currency prices may intensify domestic inflation.

A group of Iranians gathered in Stockholm for the 255th consecutive day. The rally was held with slogans supporting Prince Reza Pahlavi. The aim was to attract the attention of the Swedish public and politicians to developments in Iran.

A group of housing project buyers from the Aryan Sazeh construction company protested in front of the Army Headquarters in Tehran on Saturday, September 12. They protested the delay in delivering projects such as Setin, Padefand, Afra, Gol Maryam, Pardis Shargh, and Abshar. These projects have been left unresolved for a long time.

Hossein Noushabadi criticized the IAEA Board of Governors resolution against Iran as lacking legal validity. He described the resolution as a political move by the US and three European countries to pressure the Islamic Republic. Noushabadi also called the Board of Governors a tool for countries violating international law principles.

Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, Fakhereh Zahedi, and Shima Sanaei, three Baha'i citizens, were released from Tircola prison in Sari on bail. Zahedi was released on September 6, Sanaei on September 7, and Manouchehrzadeh on September 9. A property bail worth two billion tomans was provided for each release.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said that the US and the Islamic Republic are trying to increase the cost of conflict for the other side in the Persian Gulf. He considers the continuation of the tanker war as the most likely short-term scenario. These remarks refer to the ongoing tensions in the region.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated in an interview with India Today that the Islamic Republic is not at war with Saudi Arabia. This statement came after a drone attack on the east-west pipeline in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia and Iraq claimed the attack was launched from Iraqi territory.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to Kayhan newspaper's note about targeting oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman. He said this view believes that land, people, and the country must be sacrificed for their ideals. Akbarin described these policies as continuing the path of destruction, poverty, and ruin for the country.

On the early morning of Sunday, 22 Shahrivar, the death sentences of six prisoners were carried out in the prisons of Iranshahr, Zabol, Zahedan, and Jiroft. These prisoners were sentenced for drug-related crimes. The executions were carried out in separate cases.

The president of Alzahra University reported difficulties in finding a contractor to provide student meals due to price increases. Contractors are unwilling to cooperate at last year's prices, requiring support. Financial problems and dormitory challenges were also mentioned.

Masoud Rangrazani was shot dead on the evening of Friday, January 9, 2026, in Islamshahr, Tehran. His family decorated the place where he was killed on the street. This video was released by Iran International.

Tuition fees in private schools have increased by up to 65 percent in some areas. Families face serious financial difficulties in covering educational and living expenses. There are also reports of plainclothes and Basij forces present in some regions.

Turkey and Azerbaijan are expanding their cooperation in electricity and renewable energy. The cooperation focuses on three main projects, including electricity connection via Nakhchivan, a green electricity corridor among four countries, and a power transmission line from the Black Sea to Europe. These projects could strengthen Turkey's position in regional energy transit.

Kylian Mbappe scored a penalty in Real Madrid's match against Rayo Vallecano, bringing his goal tally in the new La Liga season to 6. He is now only 8 goals away from Cristiano Ronaldo's record of 100 goals for Real Madrid. Mbappe has the opportunity to approach this historic record with upcoming matches.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of Iranians residing in the UK gathered on Saturday, September 12, in London and Newcastle. The gathering was against the Islamic Republic. The locations of the gatherings were London and Newcastle.

The CEO of the Thalassemia Association in Kermanshah reported the increase in price and shortage of essential medicines for patients. The price of a 10-pack of Desferal has risen from 50,000 to 500,000 tomans. Additionally, imported drugs like Prolia injections are unavailable for many patients due to high prices and shortages.

Farmarz Tofighi stated that the minimum wage for workers only covers about eight days of monthly expenses, with many basic needs removed. The prices of medicine and paraclinical services have sharply increased, and housing prices in Tehran have exceeded 240 million tomans per square meter. He warned about workers migrating to neighboring countries due to lack of jobs.

Mohammad Taghi Naqdali, representative of Khomein, said the Iraqi government should know that puppet regimes are falling and the US is leaving. He emphasized that the survival of the Al-Zaidi government in Iraq depends on respecting the Resistance Front and positive interaction with the Islamic Republic. He also stressed maintaining good neighborly relations between the two countries.

The wife of Alireza Khademi, a protester killed in the December 2025 protests, participated in the memorial campaign by lighting a candle in his memory. Alireza Khademi was arrested while helping the injured and his body was returned to his family after two weeks with signs of torture. Sources close to the family reported severe injuries on his body.

Ali Mamouri, a Middle East studies researcher, said that the Houthis and the Islamic Republic currently do not intend to completely close the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This waterway remains open to ships except for Saudi vessels. This statement was made regarding the Houthis' advances in Yemen.
Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, met and talked with Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa, on the sidelines of the BRICS summit.

The Israeli army has stated it does not intend to withdraw from the Ali Taher heights. Operations against Hamas commanders and efforts to rebuild the group's military capabilities in Gaza continue. The Israeli army is on high alert on both the northern and Gaza fronts.
A woman in Tehran killed her husband by striking his head and cutting his wrist. The incident occurred on Friday, 20 Shahrivar. The woman was arrested by the police.

The founder and CEO of Anthropic warned that the rapid development of advanced AI models could lead to losing human control over this technology. This issue was discussed in an interview with Nima Dadgostar. The warning highlights the importance of managing AI development.

Branko Ivanković met with Javad Nekounam and the Tractor team staff during their camp in Dubai. He spoke with his former students and Croatian players of Tractor. Panadić is also working as the goalkeeping coach for Tractor.

589 villages in 28 counties of Khorasan Razavi are facing drinking water stress. Since the beginning of the year, over 108,000 cubic meters of water have been distributed by tanker to more than 261,000 residents. 426 villages suffer from water shortages and 71 villages have water quality issues, receiving continuous mobile water supply.

An IRIB expert, referring to the US military campaign against the Iranian government, said that Americans have repeatedly stated that by striking Islamic Republic facilities they were able to delay the emergence of Imam Mahdi.

The mother of Mehran Niayesh lit a candle for her son by joining the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." Mehran Niayesh, 37, was arrested on January 9, 2026, in Baharestan, Isfahan province, in front of his pregnant wife. His body was delivered to the family two days later after receiving 600 million tomans.

Abbas Araghchi stated that the Strait of Hormuz will not open after the agreement with Oman. The condition for reopening the strait is the US returning to its commitments under the Islamabad agreement. The agenda of the Oman meeting is a new maritime route in the Strait of Hormuz.

Employees at the Tose power plant in Mashhad report a water shortage crisis and unit closures. A Zahedan municipality engineer faces severe living conditions and cannot afford his wife's medical treatment. Additionally, there are reports of sharp price increases and healthcare difficulties.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that he cannot currently decide on direct talks with Donald Trump. Reza Talebi attributes this duality to Ali Khamenei's long-standing approach. The power of the armed forces and the IRGC in diplomacy has also increased.

The Secretary-General of the Arab League described the role of the Islamic Republic towards some Arab countries as very negative and called for a change in Tehran's policies. He stated that the conflict in the Gulf region cannot be resolved through military intervention and warned that the crisis is likely to continue. He also emphasized that Arab countries should establish clear frameworks for their relations with Iran.

The 83rd Venice Film Festival concluded after ten days with a closing ceremony and award presentations. Laleh Marzban won the best actress award in the Horizons section and dedicated it to the struggles of Iranian women. Sadaf Baghbani reported on this event.

Mojtaba Ahmadi Darani, a bachelor's student of Russian language and literature at Shahid Beheshti University, was sentenced to two semesters of suspension from studies. This sentence was issued by the university's disciplinary committee. More details were published by Harana News Agency.

The head of Tehran Chamber of Commerce stated that sanctions have become tougher and government revenues have sharply decreased. Labor activists said the poverty line has exceeded 70 million tomans. The monthly living cost for a working-class family is estimated between 80 to 90 million tomans.

Sara Musighi, a political prisoner, was sentenced to six years in prison by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. She is held in Qarchak Varamin prison and was tortured during detention. Her family reported that she was denied proper medical care.

Asieh Amini reported that many students are deprived of education due to poverty. She described this situation as a national-historical disaster. Poverty and lack of education threaten the historical achievements of Iranian society.

Retirees in Ahvaz, Shush, and Rasht protested against their living conditions and delayed social security payments. They criticized the insufficient payments and the slow, piecemeal disbursement of arrears. The retirees demanded urgent attention to their demands.

About 130,000 people, equivalent to 15% of the urban population of North Khorasan, live in 70 inefficient and informal settlements. These neighborhoods are concentrated in seven cities of the province. Additionally, about 1,600 hectares of worn-out and inefficient urban fabric have been identified in these cities.

A merchant spoke in a video about the sharp increase in car engine oil prices. He said prices have risen significantly and he does not know how to inform people about this. He expressed concern about the situation of consumers.

The Janfada Iran headquarters announced the preparation for training and organizing one thousand Janfada National Resistance battalions. This move follows widespread public support for cooperation with the armed forces. Janfada activities in other defense areas will be announced soon.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, stated that individuals who held positions in the past should not be immune from judicial action. He referred to Hassan Rouhani's positions, saying that at that time they were not seeking a referendum. The parliament has requested judicial follow-up and action against certain individuals by majority vote.
Maria Sharapova, the retired Russian tennis player, shared a photo of herself at the US Open. She won five Grand Slam titles. Sharapova won Wimbledon in 2004 at the age of 17.

Retirees from the Isfahan steel industry protested in front of the governor's office against the performance of Dana supplementary insurance and healthcare service issues. They also demanded full implementation of salary adjustments and attention to their livelihood demands. The protest took place today.

People in Sweden went to the polls on Sunday for the general election. This election will determine whether the right-wing Sweden Democrats enter the government for the first time or if power returns to the center-left coalition. An interview was conducted with Mehran Abbassian, a reporter from Iran International.

The teenage daughter of Morteza Haddad Shalkouhi lit a candle at her father's grave as part of the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign. Morteza Haddad Shalkouhi was killed on January 9, 2026, in Rasht. This video was released by Iran International.

A citizen secretly recorded a video from the flogging execution room. This video will soon be published as a detailed testimony. The purpose is to expose the injustice and humiliating punishments faced by Iranian people.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a ship was targeted in the Strait of Hormuz. The governor of Qeshm stated that one person was killed and three others injured in the incident. He identified the United States as the perpetrator of the attack.

The Tehran prosecutor has filed charges against the host, producer, and two guests of the online program "Ba Zia" for making false economic claims and unsubstantiated statements. This action was taken due to the accusations made in the program. More details have been published by Harana News Agency.

Romina Pourmokhtari was appointed as Sweden's Minister of Climate and Environment. She became the youngest minister in Sweden's history after this appointment. A special interview with her is available on Iran International's YouTube channel.

Faisal bin Farhan, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister, stated that GCC countries do not accept attacks on their territory or vital interests. He emphasized the importance of national security and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. He added that stability in these routes is crucial for energy security and global trade.

Majid Ibn al-Reza, acting defense minister, stated that the Islamic Republic would perform much more powerfully technologically in case of another war. He said the displayed defense capability is only a small part of the actual capacity. He also emphasized that the Islamic Republic relies on internal capabilities to ensure its security.

Six years ago on this day, Navid Afkari, an Iranian wrestler and protester of the August 2018 protests, was executed. The execution took place despite requests and reactions from international and human rights organizations. Navid Afkari was executed by the Iranian government on September 12, 2020.

Shahbaz Sharif, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, condemned the proxy attacks by the Islamic Republic on southern Saudi Arabia. Yahya Saree, the military spokesperson for the Houthis, confirmed the attacks using ballistic missiles and drones. The attacks targeted ammunition depots and command centers of a military base in southern Saudi Arabia.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated after the BRICS summit in New Delhi that he hopes the malicious intentions of the US in the region will be thwarted. He emphasized that BRICS countries favor a multipolar world and increased economic cooperation. Opposition to unilateral sanctions and expansion of trade with national currencies were also discussed.

Donald Trump stated that the Iran issue might end before the US midterm elections but will definitely end after them. He said Iran really wants to reach an agreement, but the deal must be right. Trump also commented that the Gulf countries' meetings with Iran are their own business.
An abandoned newborn was found in one of the streets of Nurabad in Lorestan province. This incident took place in the city of Nurabad. More details are published by Harana News Agency.
A car sank into the ground on North Ferdowsi Street in Nishapur due to land subsidence. This incident occurred because of the ground sinking. No reports of casualties have been announced.

A car sank into the ground on North Ferdowsi Street in Nishapur due to ground subsidence. This incident occurred because of changes in the land. No further details about the car or driver have been reported.

Abbas Basafa announced that newly registered cars valued over one billion tomans receive 110 liters of gasoline monthly at 10,000 tomans per liter and do not get gasoline quotas at 1,500 and 3,000 tomans rates. Newly registered cars under one billion tomans receive the normal gasoline quota. Personal passenger cars with normal quotas receive 60 liters of gasoline at 1,500 tomans and 50 liters at 3,000 tomans monthly.

Ali Sarai's brother joined the 'One Candle, One Name, One Memory' campaign and lit a candle for him. Ali Sarai was shot and killed by officers on January 9, 2026, in Azadshahr, Mashhad. His brother said his path continues.

A group of Iranians gathered in central Brussels on Sunday, September 13. The gathering was held to commemorate Mahsa Zhina Amini and those who died in the protests in Iran. It also aimed to support political prisoners and protest executions in Iran.

The German government announced a significant decrease in asylum applications. The rate of support granted to Iranian applicants after case reviews has risen to over 42 percent. This report was published by Ali Hassanpour from Iran International.
A man in Tehran was tried in criminal court for the murder of his wife and two young children. This incident took place in Tehran province. The trial of this individual is ongoing.

The coalition of political forces in Iranian Kurdistan has called on people to hold a general strike on Wednesday, September 25. This strike coincides with the fourth anniversary of the killing of Mahsa Zhina Amini and the start of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement. The coalition described the strike as a civil response to security and economic crises.

Heavy vehicle drivers are trapped at the Chazabeh border after it was closed. They have been stuck there for three days without water, food, or facilities. This was reported in a video sent to Iran International.

The war involving Iran and restrictions on tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have increased the return of the American investment fund "Breakwave Tanker Shipping" by 3600 percent. The oil shipping rates in Middle Eastern routes have risen by nearly 500 percent compared to last year. This situation is due to difficulties passing through the Strait of Hormuz and increased maritime transport costs.

Ahmad Reza Radan, the chief of police, stated that Alireza Beiranvand must choose between Malavan or Fajr Sepasi teams for his military service. He emphasized that military service is mandatory for everyone with no exceptions. The champion soldier law does not apply to Beiranvand, and he must complete his service.

Hossein Rasouli Nasab, a detainee from the December 2025 protests in Shandiz, was sentenced to death by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. His charges include waging war against God, destruction of public property, burning religious centers, and conspiracy against national security. He is currently imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Javad Hosseini, head of the Welfare Organization, said there are currently 10,350,000 elderly people in the country, making up nearly 14 percent of the population. He predicted the share of Iran's population over 60 will reach 31 percent by the year 1430. Hosseini warned that necessary facilities and programs are not in place to match the speed of aging.

The Civil Registration Organization announced that artificial intelligence and blockchain technologies have been used in the new national ID cards. This measure aims to enhance security and improve services. No further details were provided.

A citizen lit a candle in Behesht Sakineh, Karaj, in memory of protesters killed in December 2025. This was done as part of the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." He conveyed that they are remembered.

More than three thousand teenagers from Markazi province were sent to Rahian-e Noor camps in the operational areas of western Iran. This action is against Iran's commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child. Iran had pledged not to involve children in military activities.

There is widespread disruption at Iran's borders with Iraq and Turkey, affecting land trade and export routes. Truck waiting times at the borders have increased. Concerns have also been raised about reduced trade between the two countries due to US sanctions.

Mohsen Hashemi stated that officials of the Islamic Republic used metro stations as offices during the 12-day and 40-day wars. No safe places or public shelters were introduced for citizens during these wars. Additionally, a citizen's house in Vahdat Town, Karaj, was targeted in an attack in Esfand and remains destroyed.

Eight female prisoners in Iran face death sentences on political, security, and protest-related charges. Some of these death sentences have been confirmed, while others are still in preliminary stages. These sentences were issued by revolutionary courts in various cities.

Jared Kushner stated that the US government used Israel's global isolation after its attack on Hamas leaders in Doha for mediation. He described the attack as unsuccessful and causing Israel's isolation. The US used this situation to pressure and reach a ceasefire agreement.

According to Harana, at least eight female prisoners in Iran have been sentenced to death in political, security, and protest-related cases. The death sentences of two of them have been confirmed by the Supreme Court. The charges include rebellion, waging war against God, and corruption on earth.

The mother of Arya Alidoost lit a candle in the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" to honor her son. Arya Alidoost was killed on January 8, 2026, in Lahijan. His mother said that her son and his companions gave their lives for the freedom of Iran.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that the price of desmopressin has increased about fivefold in recent months. This medication is used to control excessive urination and thirst caused by antidiuretic hormone deficiency. The price increase has raised concerns.
Sheikh Zahed Shahabi, a citizen of Saqez, remains detained in Saqez prison after about six months. His situation in prison remains uncertain. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Mehdi Hashemi, a 125 kg wrestler, was severely injured in a collision with a Nissan pickup in Juybar, Mazandaran. He is currently hospitalized in intensive care in Sari and is in a coma. Hashemi suffered broken ribs, internal bleeding, and serious injuries to his skull, ribs, and lungs.

Barcelona defeated Levante 4-2 in the fifth week of La Liga with a double from Lamine Yamal and goals from Xavi Simons and Ademi. Yamal scored doubles for the third consecutive game, a feat last achieved by Messi. Barcelona recorded their fifth consecutive victory and remains unbeaten.

The New York Times reported that Hossein Taeb was the planner of the attack on ships during the Tehran-Washington ceasefire. After the attack, a verbal dispute occurred between Masoud Pezeshkian and Ahmad Vahidi. Ahmad Vahidi and the Supreme National Security Council claimed to be unaware of the attack.
A woman was arrested in Masal County for causing public disturbance on social media. She was referred to the judicial authorities. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Donald Trump stated that Iranian officials are continuously contacting for a deal with the US. He emphasized that the deal must be right and the Iran issue may end before the US midterm elections. Additionally, the IRGC warned American ships after attacks on two commercial vessels near Qeshm.

Hossein Samsami announced the uncertain fate of more than 56 million barrels of oil. Over 86 million barrels were allocated on credit to one person. Only 30 million barrels have been transferred to the final buyer.

Mohammadreza Mastan Saljouqi, a 66-year-old citizen and a war-related nerve and psychological injury victim, has been detained in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad for over 9 months without a clear status. His case's interrogation process started in Esfand 1404 at the Mashhad prosecutor's office, but no trial has been held yet. He has attended several interrogation sessions but remains in detention.

Representatives of Israel and Lebanon will meet in Rome in October to discuss a security agreement mediated by the US. The agreement aims to reduce conflicts along the border between the two countries. Additionally, the ambassadors of both countries will meet in Washington next week.

The Supreme Court confirmed the death sentence of a woman accused of murder. Additionally, five prisoners in various provinces were released from the death penalty with the consent of the victims' families. These prisoners were in Isfahan, Lorestan, Qazvin, Bandar Abbas, and Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari.

Bahman Modirzadeh, a member of the Qotur City Council in West Azerbaijan province, has been held in Khoy prison for 41 days. His situation remains uncertain. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Javad Nekounam, head coach of Tractor, said that Alireza Beiranvand's absence in the match against Shabab Al Ahli is important for the team and defense line. Nekounam mentioned Parsa Jafari as Beiranvand's replacement and expressed full confidence in his readiness. He also emphasized the importance of starting the competition well and having the best performance.
